episodes.description: S3 Ep. 2: What if confidence isn’t what you actively need to cultivate to show up boldly on stage? In this solo episode, I’m breaking down confidence by working backward from the outcome most of us want. We often tell ourselves that we need to feel confident before an audition or big performance, but confidence…

episodes.youtubeTitle: Plot Twist: I’m the Guest! Interviewed by my Life and Business Coach...

episodes.title: Befriending Performance Nerves
episodes.description: 7 tools to help you actually enjoy performing again. Performance nerves are universal, unavoidable… and often hard to manage. In this episode, I share a compassionate, practical, and research-informed approach to one of the biggest challenges we face as performers.

episodes.title: Stuck, Scattered, or Overthinking Your Prep?
episodes.description: My two-part process to help you find clarity, confidence, and calm before any big artistic event. What if preparing for a big performance didn't have to feel overwhelming, rigid, or all-consuming?
episodes.youtubeTitle: Stuck, Scattered, or Overthinking Your Prep?

episodes.title: Finding Freedom: Lauren Roth-Gómez's Journey of Self-Worth
episodes.description: A story of reconnection, self-belief, and coming home to your art. What happens when you've spent years feeling like your playing is never good enough? Violinist Lauren Roth-Gómez, Acting Associate Concertmaster of the Atlanta Symphony, shares the inner transformation that led her back to herself and her artistry.
episodes.youtubeTitle: Finding Freedom: Lauren Roth-Gómez’s Journey of Self-Worth

episodes.title: The Cost of Being Your Own Worst Critic
episodes.description: When your worth depends on your results, and how that pressure leads to burnout. If your inner-critic has been running the show — the one that tells you you're only as worthy as your latest performance, audition result, or practice session — this episode is for you. We explore the real cost of being your own worst critic and how to shift from inner-critic to inner-coach.
episodes.youtubeTitle: The Cost of Being Your Own Worst Critic

episodes.title: Inside the Genius of Joshua Smith
episodes.description: A conversation around vulnerability, long-haul artistry, and the case for communication over perfection — through the lens of a 35-year run in one of the most high-pressure chairs in the orchestral world. I sit down with Joshua Smith, Grammy-nominated Principal Flute of The Cleveland Orchestra, to explore curiosity, freedom, and sustainable excellence.
episodes.youtubeTitle: Inside the Genius of Joshua Smith

episodes.title: The Well-Being Wheel: A Whole-Human Approach to Music
episodes.description: If you've ever felt like music has taken over your entire life — the long hours, the pressure, the constant fear of not doing enough — this episode is for you. I introduce The MindfulOpus Well-Being Wheel — a framework designed to help musicians move from burnout to balance by nurturing all parts of your life.
episodes.youtubeTitle: The Well-Being Wheel: A Whole-Human Approach to Music

episodes.title: The Mindful Audition: How Feeling Good Became James Patterson's Secret to Winning
episodes.description: A conversation around mindfulness, perfectionism, well-being, and rewriting the audition story from the inside out. I sit down with James Patterson, Tredjestilling Horn (3rd/1st horn) player with the Oslo Philharmonic, to explore how he completely reimagined his approach to auditions — with his well-being front and center.
episodes.youtubeTitle: The Mindful Audition: How Feeling Good Became James Patterson’s Secret to Winning

episodes.title: The Perfection Trap
episodes.description: Are you chasing perfection...or pursuing excellence? In this episode, I dive into one of the most common — and costly — mindsets musicians face: perfectionism. I share why perfection isn't sustainable and how excellence becomes the foundation for a career and life you can sustain, with the Excellence over Perfection Framework.

episodes.title: Winning, But at What Cost?
episodes.description: In the classical music world, we're often taught that struggle is the price of greatness. But what if our artistry didn't have to come at the cost of our humanity? I take you behind the curtain of my own journey — from grueling childhood auditions in France, to winning my dream job at 21 and facing career-threatening injuries.

episodes.title: MindfulOpus Podcast Trailer
episodes.description: Hello and welcome to the MindfulOpus podcast! I'm your host, Jo Zakany — violist with The Cleveland Orchestra, yoga teacher, and coach for classical musicians. Here, we switch from Grind to Kind in our artistic process – so that artists like you can avoid burnout, ditch performance anxiety, and create a thriving, healthy life - on and off stage.
